Frequently asked questions

Common questions about adding note names to sheet music with this app. For the steps, see the guide.

Can I use it on a phone, an iPad, Safari, or Firefox?

The app is tested on Chrome and Edge 137 or later on a computer, Safari on iPhone (iOS 27.2), and Chrome on Android (137 or later). The reading engine needs a browser feature called JavaScript Promise Integration (JSPI). Browsers without it show a message instead. On an iPhone, update to iOS 27.2 or later. Firefox (153 or later) and Safari on a Mac or iPad (27 or later) have it too, but the app has not been tested on them yet, and older phones and tablets may not have enough memory for reading (about 2 GB). If it does not work, take the photo with your phone and open it on a computer.

Is it free? Do I need an account?

It is free, with no account, no sign-up, and no ads.

Is my sheet music uploaded anywhere?

No. The photo, image, or PDF is read inside your browser and is never sent to a server. Photos taken with the camera are not saved. Only the notes of the last 10 scores you opened (as MusicXML), with their titles, tempo, and transposition, are kept in the browser so you can open them again. See the privacy policy.

How long does reading take?

Roughly 10 to 60 seconds per page, depending on the device and the number of staves. The first time, the app also downloads its reading engine (about 130 MB) once; after that it starts right away and works offline.

What kind of sheet music can it read?

Printed music in standard notation: a single melody or a piano score on two staves (grand staff) works best. Images (JPEG, PNG, WebP, …) and PDFs can be read, up to 12 files at a time as one score. Handwritten music, tablature, and chord charts without notes cannot be read. Scores with many staves take longer and contain more mistakes.

How do I read a piece with several pages?

Add the photos (or PDFs) to the list one after another, up to 12 files, check the order (drag the handle to change it), and press “Read the score”: the pages are read in order and joined into one score. The pages of a PDF are read in order, and a photo of two facing pages is split and read left page first. Reading takes about a minute per page; with many pages the browser may run out of memory, especially on a phone. Then read fewer pages at a time.

Some notes are wrong. How do I fix them?

Switch to Edit and drag the notes to the right pitch and length, add missing ones, or delete extra ones. Measures marked “!” did not add up when they were read, so check those first. Many mistakes go away with a sharper, straighter photo. See how to fix reading mistakes and photo tips.

Are the sharps and flats of the key signature included?

Yes. Each name includes the key signature, the accidentals earlier in the measure, and ties over the bar line: in G major every F is named F♯. When you transpose, the names follow the new key. If the key signature itself was read wrong, every name changes with it, so compare the first line with the paper. See sharps, flats, and key signatures.

Which note names can it write?

Five systems: ドレミ (Japanese katakana), どれみ (hiragana), C D E (letters), Do Re Mi (fixed Do), and 도레미 (Korean). Choose one above the score; the first choice follows your browser's language. The names are fixed (C is always Do). Movable Do, German names (H for B), Japanese ハニホ, and octave numbers (C4) are not offered. See the note name chart.

Can it write the names inside the note heads, or color the notes?

Not yet. The names are written under the notes, like lyrics. Their size can be small, medium, or large.

Can I print it or send it to someone?

Yes. Under the score, Print prints A4 pages (choose “Save as PDF” in the print dialog for a PDF), Save image saves each page as a PNG, and Share sends the images through your phone's share menu. Each page has the title and a small “Made with Note Namer” line at the bottom, which can be turned off in the Save / share menu.

My score has lyrics. Are they kept?

The reading does not pick up lyrics or chord symbols. When you open a MusicXML file with lyrics, the screen shows only the note names in their place.

Can I open a MusicXML file I already have?

Yes. Choose or drop a .musicxml, .mxl, or .xml file and it opens right away with its tempo, without reading. Partwise MusicXML, which is what notation programs export, is supported.

Where did my last score go? How do I delete it?

The score you had open appears again when you open the app, and the last 10 scores are listed under Recent scores in the left panel. Clear history removes that list (the open score stays), and Clear removes the open score. They are also removed when you clear this site's data in the browser settings, and they are not kept in private browsing.
